title: The closed flip: the updater feed + the downloads move to the public distro repo (IUM-dist)
body:
# The closed flip: the updater feed + the downloads move to the public distro repo (IUM-dist)

**Owner decision (2026-11-11): option B — private source + public distro repo.**
The source repo `kahlanhamza/IUM` is now PRIVATE (the docs/12 private-flip procedure,
step 5, executed by the owner after the verified v0.2.1 cut). The distro repo
`kahlanhamza/IUM-dist` exists, PUBLIC, push+admin verified.

## The wire facts (measured 2026-11-11, post-flip)

- `GET https://api.github.com/repos/kahlanhamza/IUM` unauthenticated → **403** (private ✓).
- `GET https://github.com/kahlanhamza/IUM/releases/latest/download/latest.json`
  unauthenticated → **404**. THE CASUALTY: `ium-app/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` bakes that
  URL as the updater endpoint, so every shipped v0.2.0/v0.2.1 install lost auto-update
  the moment the flip landed (#100's fix is intact — the feed it now serves is just
  unreachable by the public).
- README:78 + USERGUIDE:9 point users at the source repo's Releases page — now auth-walled.
- `release.yml` publish job creates the release with `${{ github.token }}` (source-repo
  scoped; cannot write cross-repo) and builds `latest.json` with `--repo
  "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY"` → manifest asset URLs also point at the private repo.
- The publish job's release notes tell users to `gh attestation verify -R
  kahlanhamza/IUM` — the attestation store lives on the (now private) source repo, so
  that command needs auth. The offline sigstore bundles (`*.attestation.*.jsonl`,
  cosign verify-blob-attestation against Fulcio/Rekor) are PUBLIC and already ship —
  they become the primary user-facing verification path.
- `scripts/build_latest_json.py` already takes `--repo` (self-test asserts only filename
  suffixes, not the slug — the retarget does not rot the detector).

## The design (option B mechanics)

1. **IUM-dist** (public) = distribution point ONLY: releases, assets, `latest.json`.
   No source code, ever. Already has its initial commit (releases can tag).
2. **Updater endpoint** (tauri.conf.json) →
   `https://github.com/kahlanhamza/IUM-dist/releases/latest/download/latest.json`.
   Baked at build time — so the FIRST release through the new feed must be **v0.2.2**
   (patch: channel move, zero product surface).
3. **release.yml publish job**: create/upload the release on `-R kahlanhamza/IUM-dist`
   with `secrets.DISTRO_TOKEN` (a PAT with contents:write on the distro repo — set as
   an Actions secret, never printed); manifest `--repo kahlanhamza/IUM-dist`;
   attestation store STAYS on the source repo (maintainer-side; the offline bundles
   carry public verification); `contents: write` drops from the publish job's
   permissions (least privilege — it no longer touches source-repo releases).
4. **Docs**: README loses the CI badges (a private repo's badges render broken in
   public and leak workflow names), download links repoint to IUM-dist; USERGUIDE gains
   the honest migration note — **v0.2.1-or-earlier installs do ONE final manual update**
   (their baked feed URL can never work again on a private repo), then auto-update is
   permanent from v0.2.2 on.
5. **RED first**: a new `ium-app/src/distro.test.ts` (the `readme.test.ts` house
   pattern) pins the conf endpoint to the distro feed and pins the updater pubkey —
   fails at HEAD, passes after the retarget. Key continuity is the updater's trust root:
   the pubkey MUST NOT change in a channel move.
6. **Verify-before-declared** (the release bar): after the v0.2.2 tag drives the
   workflow — unauthenticated `latest.json` returns 200 with `version: 0.2.2` +
   `darwin-aarch64` key; assets present on the PUBLIC repo; one asset's sha256
   cross-checked against SHA256SUMS.txt; signature byte-identical to the `.sig` asset.

## Non-goals (unchanged owner asks)

Code signing (Apple Developer + Windows cert), OAuth client registration, paid
channels. The private vulnerability-contact channel (README security advisories now
requires source-repo access) is flagged to the owner as a follow-up owner ask.
